**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2022/09/24 (Sat) 13:37
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Posture is an important aspect of body language that refers to the way that a person stands or sits, as well as the overall position of their body.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Posture can indicate confidence, interest or attention, dominance or submission, relaxation, and health.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Illustrators are gestures used to illustrate or emphasize the words being spoken.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common examples of illustrators include pointing, gesturing, nodding, shaking head, and facial expressions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Adaptors are gestures or behaviors used to adapt to the environment or relieve stress or anxiety.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common examples of adaptors include fidgeting, self-grooming, playing with objects, touching one's face, and pacing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Regulators are body language cues used to control the flow of conversation or interaction.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of regulators include nodding to indicate agreement, shaking the head for disagreement, holding up a hand to signal a desire to speak, making eye contact to show attention, and avoiding eye contact to signal disinterest.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Displays of power refer to body language cues that convey dominance or submissiveness.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Displays of power can indicate dominance, submissiveness, status, authority, and confidence.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Flirting involves body language that signals romantic or sexual interest.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Flirting cues include making eye contact, smiling, touching hair or face, showing playfulness, and creating intimacy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Deception refers to body language cues that indicate a person is not telling the truth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Signs of deception include avoiding eye contact, fidgeting, crossing arms, lack of emotion, and inconsistencies between words and actions.
